status: Interface review; transfer constraints identified, implementation audit pending.
insights: Constant folding has explicit target DataLayout and TargetLibraryInfo dependencies. Layout-sensitive results must not be cached or reused as context-free language equalities.

LLVM permits choosing a legal nondeterministic result for some folds only when all uses are replaced. Ink exact floating bits/canonical arithmetic NaN rules require its own equality semantics; LLVM AllowNonDeterministic defaults cannot be copied into a proof producer.
Input and output denormal modes are distinct; dynamic input mode can prevent folding. A generic producer must decline unsupported semantic environments rather than silently using host arithmetic.
Loads from constant data need exact bounds, layout and value interpretation. LLVM poison/undef behavior and lossless cast refinement do not authorize Ink out-of-range or wrapping substitutions.
Math-call folding separately checks effects such as errno. Constant arguments alone do not prove purity.

Useful producer/checker design: carry explicit width/sign/layout/effect context, return no candidate when unavailable, and replay an exact Ink equality proof. Existing Ink constant-fold capabilities must be audited before adding duplicate mechanisms.
scope: Reviewed complete header declarations and documented API contracts; implementation ConstantFolding.cpp and Ink fold sites are not yet fully audited. No performance claim or implemented new optimisation.
